item.title: Why the Moonshot Moment May Not Be a DeepSeek Moment
item.description: History doesn’t always repeat itself.

item.title: Valve’s 14-Year Journey to Make the Steam Machine
item.description: The company first began laying the groundwork for this year’s hardware way back in 2012

item.title: Sateliot Expands Funding to Offer Satellite Service to Phones
item.description: Satellite startup Sateliot is seeking to boost an ongoing fundraising round to as much as €150 million ($172 million), about a 50% increase as the Spanish company aims to offer satellite connectivity directly to smartphones.

item.title: Apple in Early Settlement Talks With DOJ Over Antitrust Case
item.description: Apple Inc. and the US Justice Department are in early discussions about settling a 2024 lawsuit that alleges the iPhone maker violated antitrust laws.

item.title: Telecom Italia Is Said to Consider €10.8 Billion Poste Bid Fair
item.description: Telecom Italia SpA’s board is leaning toward endorsing Poste Italiane SpA’s €10.8 billion ($12.4 billion) takeover offer as fair, and is unlikely to seek a higher price, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Meta in Talks to Sell Computing Power to Anthropic, NYT Reports
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. is in early discussions to lease computing power from its data centers to Anthropic PBC, an arrangement that could be worth as much as $10 billion over two years, according to the New York Times.

item.title: Chile’s Government Stakes Ever More on Tax Cuts, Easing Red Tape
item.description: As Chile’s economy grinds to a halt, the government is placing ever more hopes on the impact of a bill to cut taxes and red tape. Economists are starting to get skeptical.

item.title: Sweetgreen Pares 26% Drop as Parasite Tied to Taco Bell Lettuce
item.description: Sweetgreen Inc. shares surged on Friday, halting a four-day skid, after US regulators said a parasite outbreak that’s sickened thousands across several states was traced to shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants.

item.title: Griffin Wants to Buy an Old Cottage Across From New Headquarters
item.description: Ken Griffin has gone to extraordinary lengths to assemble parcels of land around his planned Citadel headquarters in Miami, including buying up all 138 units in a condo building across the street.

item.title: US Gasoline Prices Are Heading to $4 a Gallon Again
item.description: It’s the middle of summer driving season, when Americans typically embark on road trips and burn through millions of barrels of gasoline each day. They’ll be paying more for every fill up.

item.title: How New PM Andy Burnham Affects Your Money and UK Markets: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about the UK’s new prime minister Andy Burnham and what his policies mean for your money and markets in a Live Q&A on Tuesday, July 16 at 2 p.m. BST.

item.title: Foundever Strikes Deal With Creditors to Slash Debt Load
item.description: Troubled business services giant Foundever Group has reached an agreement with a group of creditors to reduce its multi-billion dollar debt load, with the company’s controlling shareholder injecting fresh funds and installing new management.

item.title: Wild Weather Disrupts Copper Mines and Ports in Central Chile
item.description: Copper mines and ports in central Chile curtailed some operations in the face of a powerful winter storm, while major mining installations in the north remained unaffected.

item.title: Hedge Fund Blasts Settlement With SEC After ‘Gag Rule’ Lifted
item.description: Connecticut hedge fund Deccan Value Investors is speaking out about its 2022 settlement of Securities and Exchange Commission claims that it breached its fiduciary duty to two university endowments after the regulator recently lifted its so-called gag rule.

item.title: Dollar Hedging Costs Sink to Their Lowest Level This Year
item.description: The cost of hedging against swings in the dollar has fallen to its lowest level this year, signaling that traders see little chance of a major catalyst disrupting the world’s reserve currency despite an uncertain Federal Reserve outlook and resurgent conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Shakira Tax Win Set to Face Supreme Court Appeal in Spain
item.description: Shakira’s fight with Spain’s tax agency is set to head to the country’s highest court after authorities challenged an earlier ruling that had erased €55 million ($64 million) in claims against the singer.

item.title: ASML to Pay One-Time €20,000 Bonus to Staff as AI Propels Demand
item.description: ASML Holding NV will give employees globally a one-time €20,000 ($22,862) bonus, joining other firms in the chip industry to offer payouts as artificial intelligence demand fuels record sales.

item.title: Hammack Sees No Conflict in Fed’s Goals, Inflation Her Worry
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said persistently high inflation is her bigger concern as consumer spending holds up and unemployment remains low.

item.title: Anglo Selects Penny’s Group as Preferred Bidder for De Beers
item.description: Anglo American Plc has selected a group led by De Beers’ former boss Gareth Penny as the preferred bidder for its sale of the world’s biggest diamond mining company, people with knowledge of the matter said.

item.title: Bethesda Announces New ‘Fallout’ Roadmap Following Xbox Reset
item.description: The studio confirmed development on ‘Fallout 5’ and a new game with Obsidian Entertainment

item.title: US Consumer Sentiment Climbs on Cheaper Gas, Tops Forecasts
item.description: US consumer sentiment rose in early July to a five-month high as lower gasoline prices boosted morale.

item.title: BASF Seeks Banks to Lead IPO of €20 Billion Agrichemical Unit
item.description: BASF SE has invited banks to pitch for roles on an initial public offering of its agrichemical division in Frankfurt, in what could be one of the largest offerings the bourse has seen in recent years.

item.title: Apple Tops Nvidia as World’s Largest Company Amid Tech Rotation
item.description: Apple Inc. is again the biggest company in the world after wresting the title from Nvidia Corp., which has held it since May 2025.

item.title: Chips Stocks Tumble Into Bear Market as 105% AI Rally Fizzles
item.description: A closely-watched index of semiconductor stocks has fallen into a bear market, unwinding a chunk of the blistering memory-led rally that saw the gauge more than double in just three months.

item.title: US Manufacturing Output Stalls, Held Back by Durable Goods
item.description: US manufacturing production stalled in June, dragged down by a decline in durable goods such as machinery.

item.title: Hedge Fund Symmetry Gets Regulatory Nod to Operate in Dubai
item.description: Symmetry Investments has received the regulatory approval to operate in Dubai, joining hedge fund peers who’re continuing to expand in the emirate despite the regional conflict.

item.title: Spain, Portugal Data Center Boom Faces Electrical Grid Bottlenecks
item.description: Spain and Portugal are experiencing a significant data center boom, but constraints around electrical grid capacity, network access and permitting are slowing the pace of new project development.

item.title: Bank of Italy Raises Growth Forecast in Another Boon for Meloni
item.description: The Bank of Italy raised its outlook for the country’s economy, judging that a positive start to the year will outweigh fallout that followed from the Iran war.

item.title: US Housing Starts Rebound on Multifamily Construction
item.description: Housing starts in the US surged in June after a sharp drop a month earlier, driven by a rebound in apartment construction.

item.title: Brazil’s Activity Surprises on Upside Despite Cooling Outlook
item.description: Brazil’s economic activity unexpectedly accelerated in May, just as the central bank mulls whether or not to continue its easing cycle ahead of August’s meeting.
